business.name: Tee Eva's Famous Old Fashioned Pies & Pralines

ranking.name: Tee Eva's Famous Old Fashioned Pies & Pralines

text.text_excerpt: Before I ever drove by this little place off of Magazine street I read about Tee (for Auntie) Eva's in a book about famous New Orleans foods. Just picked up 24 biiiig pralines (using a groupon!). They smell so good and you can watch them being made. I love seeing the care going into them! Besides pralines, Tee Eva's makes full pies, tiny little pies (pecan, sweet potato, etc), and a variety of NOLA fair including gumbo to go.

Oh my lordy!!!! The praline's are outrageous and the snowball it's bad either. My regular spot, Hansen's, was packed. The humidity was sweltering and long story short, I was not in the mood to stand in line for 20 mins. So I remember the little shop called Tee-Eva's, had snowballs. A tiny shop, I walked into olfactory heaven. Pies, pralines and gumbo. A small lady was standing there and she had just put her bible down. I ordered a 20oz banana snowball. We started chatting and I saw the fresh pralines on the stainless counter behind her. I bought 2. She was very kind. We even shared a laugh about was it, "PEE-can" or "pa-khan". We decided it didn't matter, as long as they were plenty of th...

These are so delicious, and not sickly sweet like the places that make pralines around Bourbon Street. Also, the staff here is so sweet. Go up to the window, ask for 2-3 pralines (they're about 5 inches in diameter) and share with your loved ones (or eat all by yourself). Delicious.
